subject: PoV milestones & overage / rate-card clarity
messages:
From: Sophie Ortega <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Sanchez <miguel@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify PoV timeline + overage treatment during ramp

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re aligned on the technical fit; the remaining questions from procurement/legal are around the commercial structure for the PoV. Two specific asks from our side:  

1) Can you confirm how overage/burst pricing will be charged during the evaluation ramp? We expect to spike early as we run parallel testing (small batch production traffic). We need clarity whether spikes are billed at committed rate, a separate overage rate, or if there’s a daily cap.  

2) We want the MAP to include clear milestone dates tied to price and commit changes (e.g., when committed volume goes live, when discounts kick in). Can you send a proposed MAP with dates and sample invoice math (so procurement can see worst-case scenario)?

We’re targeting an internal close by 2026-05-07 if the MAP and SOW look good. Attached: our standard PoV checklist — happy to adapt.

Thanks,
Sophie Ortega
Head of Data Platforms
Acme Analytics

[attachment: PoV-checklist.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Ortega <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Miguel Sanchez <miguel@acmeanalytics.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify PoV timeline + overage treatment during ramp

Sophie —

Appreciate the clear asks. I’ve sketched a short MAP and attached a draft rate card + sample invoice scenarios that show a few realistic spike patterns. High-level proposal:  

- PoV window: 30 days (pilot), followed by 60-day ramp-to-production. PoV start target: 2026-04-26.
- Committed baseline: 5M tokens/month for months 1–3 after go-live.
- During PoV and first 60 days of ramp: we’ll apply a softened overage policy — overage units are billed at 1.6x the committed per-token rate (vs full overage rate on standard contracts).
- Safety guardrail: daily administrative cap at 150% of daily expected usage derived from committed baseline for the first 60 days. Spikes above that will trigger immediate notifications and we’ll work with you on mitigation — those excess tokens will be billed at 1.0x (no surcharge) up to an agreed credit threshold (see below), then 1.6x thereafter.
- Introductory credit: Redwood will provide a one-time 10% invoice credit applied to PoV month to cover test-run inefficiencies (applies only if final contract executed within 30 days of PoV completion).

Attachments included: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MAP with dates & owners), ratecard_v2.pdf, SampleInvoice-Scenario.xlsx (three spike scenarios with dollar math).

Questions for you: 1) Would Acme accept a 150% daily administrative cap for 60 days as a ramp guardrail? 2) Is the PoV 30-day window sufficient for your eval team?

If you’re good, I’ll route the MAP to our legal team and generate a simple SOW draft for signature.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
[attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, ratecard_v2.pdf, SampleInvoice-Scenario.xlsx]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Ortega <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>, Miguel Sanchez <miguel@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify PoV timeline + overage treatment during ramp

Quick internal note + reply-all so Acme sees a definitive stance.

Marcus — approved on the softened overage pricing for the PoV/ramp (1.6x) and the 10% PoV credit. We’re also comfortable adding a temporary daily safety cap at 150% for the first 60 days of production ramp, with an escalation path if they consistently breach. Please make the following explicit in the MAP:

- Escalation cadence: automatic alert at 3% above cap for more than 2 consecutive days, account manager to coordinate remediation within 24 hours.
- Billing waterfall: (a) tokens within committed baseline billed at committed rate; (b) tokens up to 150% daily cap billed at committed rate (internal absorption up to credit threshold); (c) tokens above cap billed at 1.6x.
- Legal: SOW and MAP should include a firm 30-day window for execution to qualify for the PoV credit.

Marking this as final from revenue ops. Marcus, if Acme asks for a lower overage multiplier, we can consider a phased reduction after month 3 subject to steady usage metrics.

Lauren Bishop
VP Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

[internal signature]

From: Miguel Sanchez <miguel@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sophie Ortega <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify PoV timeline + overage treatment during ramp

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement:  

1) Can you provide a concrete invoice example for a 3-week spike where daily usage hits 2.2x the committed baseline for 10 days and then returns to normal? We want to see line-item math (surcharges, credits, net due).
2) We also need the MAP to show the acceptance criteria for the PoV (sample metrics). Could you bake that into mutual_action_plan.xlsx?

We attached our procurement checklist (see inline). If we can get the sample invoice and the MAP updates by EOD tomorrow, we’ll have procurement and legal sign off and aim for the 2026-05-07 close.

Also, we’ve requested an internal SOW review — can you send the SOW-draft to our legal (cc’ed: legal@acmeanalytics.com) once it’s ready?

– Miguel

[attachment: Acme-Procurement-Checklist.docx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Ortega <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>, Miguel Sanchez <miguel@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify PoV timeline + overage treatment during ramp — sample invoice + next steps

Miguel / Sophie —

Attached is the SampleInvoice-Scenario.xlsx with a concrete example that matches the 2.2x spike scenario you described. Summary highlights:  

- Worst-case (10-day 2.2x spike): net incremental charge after applying PoV credit = ~$11,700 (spreadsheet shows day-by-day). We include both the standard overage calculation and our softened policy math so you can see delta vs a standard enterprise contract.
- MAP updated: acceptance criteria (latency <= 450ms on 95th pct, accuracy gate: NLU intent match >= 92% on eval set, and stability: <2% error rate sustained over 48 hours).
- SOW draft (SOW-draft.docx) is in progress; I’ll push to your legal and attach the DocuSign link once we have final signatures.

Action items:  
- Marcus: send final MAP with updated acceptance criteria + sample invoice (done, attached).
- Miguel/Sophie: review and confirm the 150% daily cap for first 60 days and the 10% PoV credit window (30 days post-PoV).
- Lauren/Rishi: standby for legal redlines and final pricing approval (cc’d).

If all good, let’s lock a 30-min signature call on 2026-04-28 to run through final SOW & MAP. I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to finishing this out.

Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
[attachments: SampleInvoice-Scenario.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.xlsx, ratecard_v2.pdf, SOW-draft.docx]
